## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 24 (also known as the *Saṅghāṭicāra-sikkhāpada*) is a disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating a nun's care of her robes [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a nun who leaves any of her five robes untouched for five consecutive days commits an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) that must be confessed [SuttaCentral; Bechert et al. 1997]. While the origin story itself does not mention the five-day time limit—introducing it only in the formal precept—the canonical word analysis (*padabhājaniya*) clarifies the phrase *pañcāhikaṁ saṅghāṭicāraṁ atikkāmeti* to mean that if on the fifth day a nun neither wears, puts on, nor airs any of her five monastic robes in the sun, she transgresses the rule [Bechert et al. 1997; Hüsken 1997].

Scholars note that although the compound refers to the outer cloak (*saṅghāṭi*), the canonical commentary broadens the scope to encompass the entire requisite five-robe set of a nun [Bechert et al. 1997]. In the textual transmission, the Thai edition presents the variant reading *saṅghāṭivāra* ("the time-period for the outer robe") both in the Vinaya text and its commentary, the *Samantapāsādikā* [Hüsken 1997]. Commentarial discussions in the *Samantapāsādikā* address practical dilemmas under this rule, such as non-offense scenarios where a nun is prevented from handling or exposing a valuable robe due to fear of thieves [Hüsken 1997]. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels include the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 24) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pc 24), alongside Chinese Vinaya parallels in the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 104* and its Pātimokkha) and Sarvāstivāda traditions (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 131* and its Pātimokkha) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text reuse analysis by DharmaNexus registers 379 matches with 91 Pali texts—sharing extensive procedural Vinaya phrasing particularly with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules Pc 25, Np 6, Pc 48, Pc 56, and Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Np 2—as well as cross-language alignments with Tibetan canonical Vinaya commentaries (such as the *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti*, D4112) and Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* materials [DharmaNexus].
